purpose: Replace per-term disk read buffers with one prepared-owner cursor and measure allocation, capture and complete native-index effects.

implementation.ownership: A prepared disk input owns one bounded group reader. Exactly one group lease is active at a time. Group close releases its borrow without a drain requirement; preparation close frees the reader before its private run. Memory links remain independent.
implementation.sequential: Lexical groups reuse buffered records across boundaries. Nonconsecutive/backward seeks reset coordinates and retain capacity. Interned token terms remain valid while the raw buffer is reused.
implementation.failures: Read/allocation errors make the active reader terminal for its lease. A later fresh lease resets it before retrying, preventing skipped records. Partial closes, overlapping borrows, backward seeks and injected read failures are tested.
implementation.quota: Buffer allocation uses the stable prepared owner and the same statement/host quota, with a 64-KiB maximum block. It never retains an individual borrower scratch region.
implementation.format: The persisted encoder, geometry, term order, source lanes, positions, postings and source-column formats are unchanged.

methodology.baseline: Both frozen probes use identical harness bytes and main. Baseline df04d6eeab15d16cf7f435ed68f713b9618f067f adds allocation counters and native-index measurement without shared-reader ownership; candidate enables sharing.
methodology.pairing: One excluded warmup and three alternating measured pairs per cohort. No task-owned builds, tests or cleanup overlap final measurements. Other host activity and OS caches are uncontrolled.
methodology.cohorts: Capture: English/simple diverse aliases, English diverse single binding and English repeated aliases. Native index: English/simple diverse and English repeated aliases. Each uses 65536 (memory), 65537 (just spilled) and 131072 (larger spilled) repeats under identical 512-MiB quotas.
methodology.capture_timing: Includes analysis, consumer callbacks, offsets encoding and temporary teardown. Excludes input generation, fingerprint setup, startup, output verification and final Capture teardown. Consumers are callbacks, not full postings construction.
methodology.native_index_timing: Includes complete text-segment construction from typed immutable source: postings, norms, source columns, offsets and final segment bytes. Input/root setup, hashing, independent search verification and final output destruction are excluded. Final segment bytes remain in the tracked peak. This is not Parquet scan, artifact-store publication, HTTP transport or query latency.
methodology.equivalence: Every input and complete encoded SHA-256 matches across versions and candidate materialized controls where applicable. Capture token/span digests and native-index token/analysis/reuse counts are verified; resulting segments are independently searched.
methodology.memory: Tracked allocator high-water bytes exclude immutable input/root setup and are not peak RSS. Quotas match within every comparison.
methodology.allocations: group_buffers counts successful read-buffer allocations retired with normalized offset preparation; normal disk encoding uses one instead of one per distinct term. Memory paths use zero; uninstrumented controls report null.
methodology.reads: replay_reads counts private-run physical read operations, including original replay, grouped output and retired partition runs. It measures no network requests or total bytes.
methodology.quota_controls: Separate 64-MiB capture and native-index cases must complete with matching output. Owning-token capture intentionally exhausts that quota; expected OutOfMemory is a negative capacity control, not a passing product regression test.

limitations: Current evidence distinguishes capture kernels from complete native segment construction. It establishes no complete HTTP publication, Parquet scan, cloud, archive-scale, cold-storage or RSS speedup.
Owning-token controls retain the documented CPU/memory tradeoff; shared buffering does not remove every capture overhead. Earlier observations keep their own identities.
Real-provider retention qualification remains deferred; the external 142577-row HN fixture is unavailable here; a full WASM bundle remains unqualified.
